La idea la trajo <strong>Noam Chomsky</s: The idea was brought by Noam Chomsky in 1956, and he was thinking not of computers but of human languages: he was seeking to explain how a child produces sentences it has never heard. He classified grammars into four levels by their power, and the second of them, the context-free ones, turned out to be exactly what was needed for programming languages. In 1959 John Backus and Peter Naur used a notation of that style to define ALGOL 60, and since then it has been called Backus-Naur form. It is one of the few times a linguistic theory found its application in another field and stayed there.
